site.name: Maison de la Verrière
site.concept: A candlelit Gothic refectory in the old quarter serving the cookery of medieval France, drawn from the kitchen rolls of Reims and the orchards of the Île-de-France.

card_pattern: Each menu item or module sits inside a tall pointed-arch silhouette, framed in gold-leaf line on a cobalt ground, with a Cinzel Decorative title in gold-leaf, a small fleur-de-lis ornament beneath, and Crimson Pro body text in parchment cream. Course prices are right-aligned in gold-leaf small caps. Cards are arranged in vertical arcades of three, separated by thin gold rules.
design_rules: The site reads as the inside of a stained-glass window: saturated cobalt grounds, gold-leaf line work, madder-red and verdigris accents, all separated by black 'lead came' outlines. Vertical proportions dominate — every hero, card, and image is taller than it is wide, framed by a pointed arch. Ornament is concentrated at heads, capitals, and section transitions; the body fields remain quiet, in the manner of a cathedral wall.

pages.title: Maison de la Verrière — Refectory & Cellars
pages.content_brief: Hero with a tall pointed-arch silhouette framing the wordmark and the kicker 'Founded Rue des Lombards, MCMLXXXII'. A short prose welcome from the maître d'hôtel, Henri Beauvilliers, introducing the house — twelve tables, an open hearth, a vaulted cellar of Burgundy and Loire — followed by tonight's prix-fixe in three courses (potage de châtaignes, perdreau aux coings, tarte au verjus), a rose-window centerpiece, and brief signposts to Carte, Cellier, Histoire, and Réservations.

pages.title: La Carte — Maison de la Verrière
pages.content_brief: The full carte arranged in three arcades: Entrées (œufs en cocotte au safran, terrine de lièvre à l'ancienne, soupe à l'oignon gratinée à la mie de Reims), Plats (canard rôti aux figues noires, brochet au beurre blanc, épaule d'agneau aux herbes du potager, civet de cerf), and Desserts (poire pochée au vin de Cahors, tarte fine aux pommes de Calville, blanc-manger aux amandes de Provence). Each item carries a one-line description in Crimson Pro and a price in livres-style numerals.

pages.title: Le Cellier — Wines & Provisions
pages.content_brief: The cellar list, organized by region: Bourgogne (Gevrey-Chambertin 2017, Meursault Les Charmes 2019, Chablis Premier Cru Vaillons 2020), Loire (Sancerre Domaine Vacheron, Chinon Bernard Baudry, Vouvray Huet demi-sec), Champagne (Larmandier-Bernier Latitude, Egly-Ouriet Brut Tradition), and a short list of eaux-de-vie and ratafias from convent stills. Brief paragraph on the cellar — vaulted, 13°C year-round, eleven hundred bottles deep — and a note that corkage is offered on Tuesdays only.

pages.title: Histoire de la Maison
pages.content_brief: Story of the building — a former chapter-house annex on Rue des Lombards, restored in 1982 by chef-patron Mathilde Charpentier after eleven years at La Tour d'Argent. The kitchen draws from medieval kitchen rolls, Taillevent's Viandier, and the orchards of the Vexin. Notes on the dining room: ribbed plaster vault, oak refectory tables from a dissolved priory near Soissons, eighty-four candles lit nightly. A short staff list — Mathilde Charpentier (chef), Henri Beauvilliers (maître d'), Sœur-Anne Lefèvre (pâtissière), Olivier Tassin (sommelier).

pages.title: Banquets Privés & Vœux
pages.content_brief: Private dining in the Salle Sainte-Geneviève (eighteen covers, single long table, vaulted ceiling, dedicated hearth) and the Petit Cellier (eight covers, below-stairs, lit only by candle). Three banquet menus — Menu de la Saint-Michel (autumn, six courses), Menu des Rois (winter, seven courses with galette), Menu de la Pentecôte (spring, five courses with lamb). Note that wedding luncheons and baptismal suppers are accepted with eight weeks' notice; a deposit of three hundred euros holds the room.

pages.title: Réservations & Adresse
pages.content_brief: Reservation guidance — the house seats from 19h00 until 22h30, Tuesday through Saturday; closed Sundays, Mondays, and the first fortnight of August. Telephone +33 1 42 78 14 09, or write to the maître d' at reservations@maisonverriere.fr. Address: 14 Rue des Lombards, 75004 Paris, Métro Châtelet or Hôtel-de-Ville. Closing paragraph notes the dress code (jacket preferred, no requirement) and the small twelve-seat bar that takes walk-ins from 18h30.
